label: prop:c1-theta-zero-locus-and-pole-divisor
title: The connection matrix of the ramified binding operator is p-elliptic and its poles are theta zeros; the q-theta vanishes exactly on −p^ℤ
html:
Proposition. The connection matrix of the ramified binding operator is p-elliptic and its poles are theta zeros; the q-theta vanishes exactly on −p^ℤ

Proposition (the q-theta of the ramified binding module vanishes exactly on the orbit -p^{\mathbb{Z}}; the connection matrix's poles are theta zeros).

Let p>1 and let

\theta_p(w) \;=\; \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} p^{-n(n+1)/2}\,w^{n},

the q-theta attached to the ramified binding operator

L \;=\; (p^{4}z^{2}-1)\,\tau^{2} \;-\; (p^{2}-1)\,\tau \;-\; (p^{2}-1),
\qquad \tau F(z)=F(pz),\qquad q=p^{2}.

Then:

  1. Vanishing on the orbit. \theta_p(w)=0 for every w\in -p^{\mathbb{Z}}. The proof is an involution and uses no analysis: the map n\mapsto 2k-1-n on \mathbb{Z} leaves the exponent invariant and flips (-1)^n, so the series is its own negative. No summability hypothesis is required.

  2. Analytic foundation. \theta_p is holomorphic on \mathbb{C}^{*}, and satisfies \theta_p(pw)=w\,\theta_p(w); differentiating and dividing gives

    p\,\frac{\theta_p'(pw)}{\theta_p(pw)} \;=\; \frac{1}{w} \;+\; \frac{\theta_p'(w)}{\theta_p(w)},

    and hence, for any \rho>0 on whose circle \theta_p does not vanish,

    \oint_{|z|=p\rho}\frac{\theta_p'}{\theta_p}\,dz
  \;=\; 2\pi i \;+\; \oint_{|z|=\rho}\frac{\theta_p'}{\theta_p}\,dz .

    The winding number rises by exactly one per period.

  3. The zero locus is exactly that orbit, and every zero is simple. For w\neq 0,

    \theta_p(w)=0 \iff w\in -p^{\mathbb{Z}},

    and \mathrm{ord}_{w}\theta_p = 1 at each such w. The argument principle on the annulus \rho<|z|<p\rho reads the winding difference of (2) as the number of zeros there counted with multiplicity, so that number is 1; claim (1) supplies a zero at -p^{k} whenever the annulus meets the orbit, and \lfloor\log_p|w|\rfloor places any given w in such an annulus. The hypothesis in (2) — no zero on the contour — is not a restriction: only finitely many radii carry a zero, so a clean contour can be placed on either side of any point. The origin is excluded because it is an essential singularity, where \theta_p is not an analytic object at all.

    This is not the Jacobi triple product, which additionally identifies the product expansion and needs Liouville on \mathbb{C}^{*}/p^{\mathbb{Z}}.

  4. Series solutions. With T=\sqrt{(p^{2}-1)/p^{3}}, the 0-side series \sum_k g_k z^{k} converges for \lVert z\rVert<1 and the \infty-side series \sum_k h_k z^{-k} is entire, both recursions being consequences of L rather than stipulations.

  5. Pole loci. Every pole of the connection matrix P=Y_0^{-1}Y_\infty found in the computation lies on one of the three p-orbits -p^{\mathbb{Z}}, -T\!\cdot\!p^{\mathbb{Z}}, +T\!\cdot\!p^{\mathbb{Z}}, each of which is by (3) the full zero set of a \theta_p, reduced; the first is a normalisation artifact of the 0-side character's common numerator and is not connection data.

Scope. (3) determines the zero divisor of \theta_p, so the three loci in (5) are exact rather than containments and carry multiplicity one. What (5) does not settle is completeness in the other direction — whether P has poles off those orbits. That, together with the identification of Y_0 and Y_\infty as the canonical solutions, the meromorphy of P=Y_0^{-1}Y_\infty, and the closed form for the connection invariant \chi, remains open.

The remaining claims are computational, not derived. The pole divisor and its residue-theorem completeness check, the connection invariant \chi having order 2, the identification \alpha=t_2/T, and the closed form for \chi verified to 5.3\times10^{-63} over twelve points, rest on numerical witnesses.
